'''Lawrence Mark Lidsky''' (1935–2002) was a professor of [[nuclear engineering]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT).<ref name="globe"/><ref name="mit-obit"/>

Lidsky was born in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York (state)|New York]], on October 15, 1935.<ref name="mit-obit"/> He did his undergraduate studies at [[Cornell University]], graduating in 1958,<ref name="globe"/><ref name="mit-obit"/> and earned a doctorate in nuclear engineering from MIT in 1962 with a thesis entitled "Plasma Generation and Acceleration",<ref name="mit-obit"/> after which he joined the MIT faculty.<ref name="globe"/><ref name="mit-obit"/>

Lidsky was the advisor to more than 80 graduate students and the founding editor of the ''Journal of Fusion Energy''.<ref name="mit-obit"/> In 1983, as assistant director for the MIT Plasma Fusion Center, Lidsky wrote an influential article about the difficulties of making a working [[nuclear fusion]] power plant.<ref name="globe"/><ref name="mit-obit"/><ref>{{citation|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1891&dat=19831003&id=NKofAAAAIBAJ&sjid=fNYEAAAAIBAJ&pg=1096,870419|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|title=MIT prof says fusion won't work as energy source|first=Daniel Q.|last=Haney|date=October 3, 1983}}.</ref> The ensuing reduction in federal funding for fusion research led him to resign from the center,<ref name="globe"/><ref name="mit-obit"/> and caused him to be "drummed out" of the nuclear fusion research community.<ref>{{citation|title=40-Year Effort to Harness Fusion Energy Generates New Skepticism|first=Thomas W.|last=Lippman|date=April 21, 1992|newspaper=[[Washington Post]]|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-1001865.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140629090013/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-1001865.html|via=[[HighBeam Research]]|url-access=subscription|url-status=usurped|archive-date=June 29, 2014}}.</ref>

Because of his concerns with the viability of fusion power, he instead became by 1989 an advocate for safer [[nuclear fission]] reactor designs.<ref name="globe"/><ref name="mit-obit"/><ref>{{citation|title=Return of the Nukes? Small, Gas-cooled Reactors are Billed as Safer, Cheaper|journal=[[Boston Globe]]|date=April 11, 1989|first=Larry|last=Tye|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-8115977.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140629090007/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-8115977.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=June 29, 2014|via=HighBeam Research|url-access=subscription|location=Boston, MA|quote=No one is working harder to tap that new interest than Lawrence Lidsky, a professor of nuclear engineering at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.}}</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tZ554ehDvSgC&pg=PA58|journal=[[New Scientist]]|title=Nuclear safety: some like it hot|date=November 4, 1989|pages=58–61|first=Dan|last=Charles}}.</ref>  In 1999 he was named a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] "for outstanding contributions to both nuclear fission and fusion in education, research, system design and analysis, technical publications and federal policy".<ref name="mit-obit"/><ref>{{citation|title=Eight MIT faculty and staff named Fellows of AAAS|journal=MIT News|date=December 8, 1999|url=http://newsoffice.mit.edu/1999/aaas-1208}}.</ref>

He died March 1, 2002, in [[Newton, Massachusetts]], after struggling with cancer for many years.<ref name="globe">{{citation|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-7701630.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140629090010/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-7701630.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=June 29, 2014|journal=[[Boston Globe]]|date=March 7, 2002|first=Thomas|last=Long|via=HighBeam Research|url-access=subscription|location=Boston, MA|title=Lawrence M. Lidsky; Exposed Problems with Fusion Energy}}.</ref><ref name="mit-obit">{{citation|url=http://newsoffice.mit.edu/2002/lidsky|title=Retired MIT Professor Lidsky dies; questioned fusion power research|date=March 5, 2002|journal=MIT News}}.</ref>
